noeuds.schema: Inputs: Who speaks, Emotion, The line, Place on screen, Character entrance, Effect, Sound or voice, Next comes  →  Output: Then
noeuds.role: Dialogue game: the chosen character says the line in a dialogue box, letter by letter, and the player taps the screen to continue. The character appears with their emotion (their Character sheet: pictures, color, voice). Special words: [c]color[/c], [t]shake[/t], [o]wave[/o], [p] for a pause, {score} for a variable; "🌐 9 languages" button to translate.
noeuds.exemple: Hana (happy) says "Hello!", then “Ask a choice” offers two answers.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Who asks, Emotion, Question (optional), Answer 1, Answer 2, Answer 3, Answer 4, Condition of answer 1, Condition of answer 2, Condition of answer 3, Condition of answer 4, Answer not allowed, Picture for answer 1 (optional), Picture for answer 2 (optional), Picture for answer 3 (optional), Picture for answer 4 (optional), Timer (seconds, 0 = none)  →  Outputs: Answer 1 / Answer 2 / Answer 3 / Answer 4 / Time's up
noeuds.role: Shows 2 to 4 answers as big buttons: each answer goes out through its own output, so the story branches like a tree. An answer can require a condition (otherwise it is greyed out or hidden); an optional timer adds the "Time's up" output. Each answer can also have a picture (advanced settings): the answers become big illustrated cards.
noeuds.exemple: "Open the treasure" leads to the good ending, "Leave" to the sad one.

noeuds.role: Puts a picture as the background, full screen, behind the story's characters (fading or at once). Empty picture = no more background.
noeuds.exemple: the meadow at the start, then the forest when Hana goes looking for her cat.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Character, They…, Emotion, Place on screen, Character entrance
noeuds.role: Brings a story character in (emotion, place, entrance: fade, slide, jump), changes their emotion or makes them leave, without speaking.
noeuds.exemple: Lyn comes in from the right while Hana is talking.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Character, Move to…, Size (100 = normal, 120 = bigger), Number of little jumps, Duration (seconds), Movement style, Shake (it trembles), Wait for the end before continuing
noeuds.role: Animates a character already on screen: it slides to another place, grows or shrinks, does little jumps or shakes. You set the duration and the style (even, smooth, quick then soft, slight overshoot, bounce). "Wait for the end" holds the story until the movement is over; otherwise the story goes on while it moves. The character must have been shown first with “Show / hide a character”.
noeuds.exemple: Hana slides from left to right with a bounce while she says "Wait for me!".

noeuds.role: Switches to "novel mode": the text fills the whole screen over a darkened background and the lines of “Say a line” pile up one under the other, like in a book. When the page is full, it turns by itself. "New page" clears it right away; "Back to the dialogue box" brings back the usual box.
noeuds.exemple: A night-time narration in novel mode, then back to the dialogue box for the conversation.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: What to do?, Who writes to you (name and photo on top), Who is "me" (their lines on the right), Text under the name (empty = "online")
noeuds.role: Shows the conversation as text messages on a phone: the lines of “Say a line” become bubbles (on the left for whoever writes, with three little dots "…" before they appear) and the answers of “Ask a choice” are picked at the bottom of the phone, then arrive on the right. The narrator writes a small caption in the middle (for example "Last night, 10:14 pm"). "Who writes to you" gives the name and photo at the top; "Who is me" makes a character write on the right without going through a choice. "Clear the conversation" empties the phone; "Back to the dialogue box" leaves the mode. Everything is set in the Dialogue style: colours, size, time of the "…", full-screen phone…
noeuds.exemple: SMS mode (turn on, who writes to you: Hana) → Say a line (Hana: "Are you there?") → Ask a choice ("Yes, tell me" / "Why?").

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Achievement name, Description (shown in the list), Achievement image (empty = a star), Hint while it is hidden (empty = none)
noeuds.role: Unlocks an achievement: an "Achievement unlocked!" banner slides in at the top of the screen (only the first time in the published game; every time in the editor so you can see it). The achievement joins the "Achievements" tab of "Endings and gallery" of the “Story title screen”: it stays hidden behind "???" (with a hint if you write one) until it is won. Put one at the end of a story, in a secret branch, after “Friendship (hearts)”… The banner is set in the Dialogue style: colours, frame image, time, place (top or bottom), sound.
noeuds.exemple: End the story (ending "The lost sock") → Unlock an achievement (name "The lost sock", description "Secret ending found").

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Start or end of the scene, Scene name (gallery)
noeuds.role: Marks a scene the player can watch again from "Endings and gallery" of the “Story title screen” ("Scenes to replay" tab). Put one at the "Start of the scene": when the story passes it, the scene unlocks and the state of the story is remembered. Put another at the "End of the scene": when replaying, the story stops there and goes back to the gallery. Nothing is saved during a replay. Music started with “Play music” also unlocks in the "Music" tab.
noeuds.exemple: "The clearing": one node at the start of the meeting with Hana, another right after she leaves.

noeuds.schema: Input: Ending name (optional: it counts in "Endings and gallery")
noeuds.role: Clears the dialogue box, the characters and the background of the story: the game takes over again. If you give an "Ending name", this ending is remembered forever and counts in "Endings and gallery" of the “Story title screen”; the saved game is erased.
noeuds.exemple: "Friends of the cabin" after the last line, then back to the title screen.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Who?, Hearts to add (−1 to remove), Maximum number of hearts
noeuds.role: Adds (or removes, with −1) friendship hearts for a character, up to the maximum. The hearts show at the top left during the story and a “+1 ❤” floats up (they can be hidden in the Dialogue style). They are saved with the game and restored by ◀ Back.
noeuds.exemple: after the kind answer “I'll stay with you”: Hana +1.

noeuds.role: Picks how the story goes on from a character's friendship hearts: the “True” output if the comparison is true, otherwise “False”. For an ending that depends on how you treated the characters.
noeuds.exemple: if Hana's friendship is at least 4 → the happy ending, otherwise the sad one.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Story title, Background picture (empty = the current background)  →  Output: New game
noeuds.role: Shows the story title over a picture, with big buttons: "Continue" (resumes where the player left off, with the background, characters, music and variables: the story saves itself at every line), "New game" (the output: the start of the story) and "Endings and gallery" (endings found and backgrounds already seen, the others are locked). During the story, the ◀ Back button returns to the previous line, even before a choice.
noeuds.exemple: placed right after "At start"; every “End the story” comes back to it.

noeuds.nom: Ask the player for a text (name…)
noeuds.role: Opens a small window with the keyboard: the player types a text (their name…), stored in the chosen variable; it continues when they tap OK. In lines, {prenom} shows this text.
noeuds.exemple: "What's your name?" → variable prenom → “Say a line” "Nice to meet you, {prenom}!".
